references.text: The priests shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God, for they present the Lord's food offerings, the bread of their God. Therefore they shall be holy.
You shall not profane my holy name, that I may be hallowed among the people of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
You shall not profane the name of your God by giving any of your children to Molech. I am the Lord.
You shall not swear falsely by my name, thus profaning the name of your God. I am the Lord.
The Nazirite vow involves keeping away from certain things and being consecrated to the Lord, just as priests were to keep themselves separate from holy offerings when they were unclean.
The Lord rebukes Israel for having profaned his holy name among the nations, and promises to hallow his great name.
Judah has profaned the sanctuary of the Lord which he loves by marrying the daughter of a foreign god.
Aaron's priestly garment with the gold plate on the turban bears the inscription 'Holy to the Lord' and shall bear the guilt for the holy offerings that the Israelites consecrate.
